title: Bargain for a multi-enterprise agreement when an authorisation covers the employer
what: Unions and bargaining representatives may ask the Fair Work Commission to authorise bargaining for an agreement covering several employers; an employer named in a supported or single-interest authorisation must bargain under it.

sources.title: Fair Work Act 2009
sources.quote: 242 Supported bargaining authorisations (1) The following persons may apply to the FWC for an authorisation (a supported bargaining authorisation) under section 243 in relation to a proposed multi-enterprise agreement: (a) a bargaining representative for the agreement; (b) an employee organisation that is entitled to represent the industrial interests of an employee in relation to work to be performed under the agreement.

confidence_note: The quote is the authorisation power; the employer's duty to bargain follows from the authorisation (not quoted here).

assessment.summary: New bargaining streams let one agreement cover several employers. It may lift pay in low-paid care sectors but sets common terms across competing employers and reduces firms' flexibility to organise work.

marks.reason: Common terms across employers reduce firms' flexibility to match pay and job design to their own productivity.
Competing employers bargaining together on labour costs dampens rivalry between them.
